--- title: "[BuckleyJames]{.doc-object-name .doc-class .doc-label .doc-label-class}" body-classes: doc-api-page page-navigation: false html-table-processing: none --- ::: {.doc-subject} Buckley-James rank-based accelerated failure time regression. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_buckley_james.py#L108-L458){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.CLASS} ```python BuckleyJames( *, max_iter=200, tol=1e-06, n_boot=None, seed=None, conf_level=0.95 ) ``` ::: ::: {.doc-text} Fits $\log(T) = X\beta + \varepsilon$ without assuming a distribution for $\varepsilon$, by alternating Kaplan-Meier-based imputation of censored log-times with ordinary least squares refitting until $\beta$ stabilizes. This is a semiparametric alternative to `AFT`: it avoids committing to a parametric error distribution, at the cost of an iterative fit, occasional slow or oscillating convergence, and no closed-form standard errors (available here only via optional bootstrap resampling, `n_boot=`). When there is no censoring at all, every residual is exact and the algorithm converges in a single step to the ordinary least squares fit of $\log(T)$ on $X$. ::: ## Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [max_iter]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[200]{.dv}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Maximum number of Buckley-James iterations (default `200`). [tol]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[1e-06]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Convergence tolerance on the largest change in any coefficient between iterations (default `1e-6`). [n_boot]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Number of bootstrap resamples for standard errors and confidence intervals. If `None` (the default), `std_error_`{.gd-no-link}, `conf_low_`{.gd-no-link}, and `conf_high_`{.gd-no-link} are `nan` (Buckley-James has no closed-form variance). [seed]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [int | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Random seed for bootstrap resampling (ignored if `n_boot` is `None`). [conf_level]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [float]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [[0.95]{.fl}]{.doc-parameter-default} : Confidence level for bootstrap coefficient intervals (default `0.95`). ::: ## Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [Fitted estimator]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : Call `~~greenwood.BuckleyJames.fit()` to produce a fitted estimator with cached results (`coef_`, `std_error_`{.gd-no-link}, `z_`, `p_value_`, `conf_low_`{.gd-no-link}, `conf_high_`{.gd-no-link}, `n_iter_`, `converged_`, `loglik_`-free since there is no likelihood), accessible as arrays or exported to DataFrames. ::: ## Details {.doc-details} Call `fit(surv, covariates)` with a right-censored `Surv` response and a covariate design (a 2-D array, a dataframe, or a formula string with `data`). An intercept is added automatically. ## Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#1b72feb5 .cell execution_count=1} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw # Load the data lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") # Fit a Buckley-James model bj = gw.BuckleyJames().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex", data=lung) bj ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=1} ``` BuckleyJames (rank-based accelerated failure time regression) coef se(coef) z p (Intercept) 6.379 NA NA NA age -0.02306 NA NA NA sex 0.4912 NA NA NA n = 228, events = 165 iterations = 13, converged = True ``` ::: ::: ## Methods {.doc-methods}
Name Description
fit() Fit the Buckley-James model to survival data.
predict() Predict the linear predictor or survival probabilities from the fitted model.
to_frame() Return the coefficient table as a DataFrame.
### [fit()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Fit the Buckley-James model to survival data. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_buckley_james.py#L208-L343){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python fit(surv, covariates=None, *, data=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [surv]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Surv | Outcome | str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : A right-censored `Surv` response, built with `gw.Surv(time=..., event=...)`. An `Outcome` or a formula string such as `'Surv(time, status == 2) ~ age + sex'` is also accepted, with its columns read from `data`. The right-hand side sets `covariates`. [covariates]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A dataframe (pandas or polars), a 2-D array, or a formula string (e.g., `"age + sex"`) evaluated against the `data` argument. A list of column names in `data` also works. [data]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : A data frame (pandas, Polars, PyArrow, DuckDB, a lazy frame, ...) holding the columns named by the response and `covariates`. When `surv`{.gd-no-link} is an `Outcome` or a formula, rows with a missing value in any column used are dropped before fitting. Covariate formula strings and lists of column names are also resolved here. ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [BuckleyJames]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : The fitted estimator itself (for method chaining) with cached coefficient arrays (`coef_`, `std_error_`{.gd-no-link}, `z_`, `p_value_`) and convergence diagnostics (`n_iter_`, `converged_`). ::: #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#8bc929b3 .cell execution_count=2} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") bj = gw.BuckleyJames().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex", data=lung) bj ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=2} ``` BuckleyJames (rank-based accelerated failure time regression) coef se(coef) z p (Intercept) 6.379 NA NA NA age -0.02306 NA NA NA sex 0.4912 NA NA NA n = 228, events = 165 iterations = 13, converged = True ``` ::: ::: ### [predict()]{.doc-object-name .doc-function .doc-label .doc-label-method} ::: {.doc-subject} Predict the linear predictor or survival probabilities from the fitted model. ::: ::: {.doc-usage-source} Usage [Source](https://github.com/rich-iannone/greenwood/blob/main/greenwood/_buckley_james.py#L351-L418){target="_blank" rel="noopener"} ::: ::: {.doc-signature .doc-Kind.FUNCTION} ```python predict(newdata=None, *, type="survival", times=None, format=None) ``` ::: #### Parameters {.doc-parameters} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [newdata]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Covariate values for prediction. A DataFrame (Pandas or Polars), 2-D array, or `None` (the default, uses the training data). A data frame may also hold other columns. The covariates are picked out by name and coded as they were at fit time, so the frame the model was fit on can be passed as is. [type]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [["survival"]{.st}]{.doc-parameter-default} : `"survival"` (default): survival probabilities $S(t \mid x)$ at `times`, evaluated by shifting the fitted residual Kaplan-Meier curve by each subject's linear predictor. `"lp"`: the linear predictor $X\beta$ (log-time location) only; returns an array. [times]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [Any]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Query times for `type="survival"` (ignored for `"lp"`). Required for `"survival"`. [format]{.doc-parameter-name}[:]{.doc-parameter-annotation-sep} [str | None]{.doc-parameter-annotation} [=]{.doc-parameter-default-sep .op} [None]{.doc-parameter-default} : Output format for `type="survival"`: `None` (auto-detect), `"pandas"`, `"polars"`, or `"pyarrow"`. Ignored for `type="lp"` (which always returns an array). ::: #### Returns {.doc-returns} ::: {.doc-definition-items} [ndarray or DataFrame]{.doc-parameter-annotation} : An array of shape `(n_subjects,)` for `type="lp"`. A DataFrame with a `time` column and one column per subject for `type="survival"`. ::: #### Details {.doc-details} Because Buckley-James makes no distributional assumption, survival predictions reuse the empirical Kaplan-Meier curve of the fitted residuals rather than a closed-form survival function: $S(t \mid x) = \hat{S}_{\text{resid}}(\log t - x^\top\hat\beta)$. This curve is only as reliable as the residual sample size and is not smooth like `AFT`'s or `RoystonParmar`'s predictions. #### Examples {.doc-examples} ::: {#010f95cd .cell execution_count=3} ``` {.python .cell-code} import greenwood as gw lung = gw.load_dataset("lung", backend="polars") bj = gw.BuckleyJames().fit("Surv(time, status) ~ age + sex", data=lung) bj.predict(lung[:2], type="survival", times=[180, 365, 730], format="polars") ``` ::: {.cell-output .cell-output-display execution_count=3} ```{=html}
